references.text: Parallel text describing how the children of Israel broke camp when the cloud lifted from the tabernacle, and how they encamped when the cloud stopped. The cloud directed their journey.
Describes the first instance when the cloud lifted from the Tabernacle of the Testimony, and the children of Israel broke camp from the Wilderness of Sinai.
The Lord's cloud was over them by day when they broke camp, showing God's guidance through the cloud.
The Lord went before them in a pillar of cloud by day to show them the way. The pillar of cloud did not depart from the people.
Context describing how the cloud covered the tent of meeting and the glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle.
Continuation explaining that when the cloud did not lift, they did not break camp, and that the fire of the Lord was in the cloud by night.
Moses reminds the people how the Lord went before them on the way to find places to camp, in fire by night and in a cloud by day.
The cloud filled the house of the Lord when the priests came out of the holy place, parallel to God's glory in the tabernacle.
The psalm describes how God led the people with a cloud by day and with the light of fire all through the night.
He spread out a cloud as a covering, and fire to give light at night - a poetic reference to God's guidance.
The prophecy that the Lord will create a cloud by day and smoke and the shining of a flaming fire by night over Mount Zion.
Paul refers to how all the fathers were under the cloud and all passed through the sea, as typology for baptism.
Confirms the principle that the movement of the cloud (up or down) is the only authority for Israel's journey.
Expands the understanding that both short-term and long-term stays are just as much God's will as the journey itself.
Complements the source verse by defining the theology behind waiting when the cloud does not lift.
The most direct parallel confirming the immediate connection between the movement of the cloud and the people's actions.
Confirms that even short waiting periods are governed by the same divine principles as long journeys.
Describes a concrete historical fulfillment of the principle that the cloud directs the route of travel.
Specifies the exact moment when the principle of the cloud's movement was put into practice.
